name: The Unlikely Collab

pick.label: Pick a brand
pick.heading: Pick a brand and find it a partner
lead: Brands love working together. Some pairs make perfect sense, like a phone and a music app. Others look like two people who met at three in the morning and decided to start a business.
Choose a brand from the shelf, or one of your own, and find it the most unlikely partner you can. Then tell us what they make together and why it works. *The stranger the couple, the better.*
pick.hint: Or click one to choose it.
pick.note: Obviously I am not looking for a serious marketing plan here, this is just for a bit of fun. Some collabs are genius, and some are just a T-shirt with two logos on it. Both are welcome, but genius gets more points.

rows: Another brand from a completely different world.
What exactly is it? A product, a menu, a shop, a range, something completely mad?
Who buys it? Fans of one brand, fans of both, people who’ve never heard of either?
Why do they need each other? Fame, cool, quality, a laugh…
Where and how does it go on sale, and how do people find out?

values.product: The Bin Day Sandal: an orange cork sandal with a reflective strap, for people who take the bins out in their socks at seven in the morning.
values.who: Berliners who are secretly proud of their bin collection, and tourists who already bought the orange T-shirt.
values.brings: The BSR brings the jokes and the orange; Birkenstock brings the comfort and a grown-up price.
values.launch: From the back of a bin lorry that drives round Kreuzberg all day. You find it by following the bin people on Instagram.

yours.label: Your collab
yours.heading: Your idea
yours.lead: Fill it in on your own phone or laptop (it stays on your device), and be ready to tell the class about your collab in a few sentences.

rank.label: The ranking
rank.heading: Which collab wins?
rank.placeholder: The collab, e.g. BSR x Birkenstock
rank.lead: Each student tells us about their collab in a few sentences. Add it, then argue it into place until everybody agrees.
